title: GOD ANSWERS STRIFE WITH A SIGN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Speak to the Israelites and get twelve staffs from them, one from the leader of each of their ancestral tribes. Write the name of each man on his staff. On the staff of Levi write Aaron's name, for there must be one staff for the head of each ancestral tribe. Place them in the tent of meeting in front of the ark of the covenant law, where I meet with you. The staff belonging to the man I choose will sprout, and I will rid myself of this constant grumbling against you by the Israelites." — Num 17:1-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the conflict of the previous chapter — the rebellion, the judgment, the grumbling that would not stop — God does something surprisingly gentle. Rather than more fire or plague, He proposes a quiet sign: twelve staffs laid before Him, and the one He chooses will sprout. God stoops to settle the dispute in a way the people can see and understand.

There is tenderness in this. God knew the constant grumbling was tearing at the community, and He moved to end it — not merely by silencing the people, but by giving them clear, undeniable evidence of His choice. He did not owe them proof. Yet in mercy He provided it, to put the question to rest once and for all.

A staff is a dead piece of wood. For one to sprout would be nothing less than a miracle, life coming from lifelessness. God would settle the matter of the priesthood not by argument but by displaying His power to bring life where there was none. His choices are confirmed by His own hand.

This is how God often works with us. When our hearts are restless and doubting, He is patient, giving us reasons to trust Him. And the greatest sign He has ever given is life from death — not a sprouting staff, but the empty tomb. Just as He confirmed Aaron by bringing life from dead wood, He confirmed His Son by raising Him from the dead. When you wonder whether God is truly at work, look to the resurrection: the sign that settles every question.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How has God patiently given you reasons to trust Him in seasons of doubt?
2. What does it mean that God brings life out of lifeless things?
3. How does the resurrection settle your deepest questions about God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are patient with my doubts and gracious to confirm Your ways. Thank You for the greatest sign of all, life from death in the resurrection of Christ. Help me to trust the God who brings life where there was none. Amen.
